title.narrative: Improved capacity of constituents to promote fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative:
Pakistan faces interconnected challenges of widespread informality, rural underemployment, gender inequality, weak enforcement of labour standards, and workplace vulnerability, all of which limit inclusive growth and social justice. This country priority aims to strengthen the capacity of government and social partners to advance fundamental principles and rights at work, expand decent employmentâ€”particularly in rural areasâ€”and promote gender equality, inclusion and safe working environments.
Efforts will focus on improving implementation of labour laws in line with ratified ILO Conventions, reinforcing labour inspection systems, strengthening social dialogue, and promoting responsible business conduct. Particular attention will be given to high-risk and informal sectors where gaps persist in freedom of association, non-discrimination, occupational safety and health, and child labour prevention. Enhanced tripartite engagement and accountability will support more effective labour governance and compliance.
In rural areas, where poverty, informality and climate vulnerability are concentrated, support will enhance national and provincial capacities to design employment strategies that promote productivity, skills development, enterprise growth, value-chain upgrading, formalization and access to social protection. Emphasis will be placed on green and climate-resilient livelihoods and improved labour standards in agriculture and rural industries.
Reducing gender gaps in labour force participation, wages and leadership is central to this priority. Interventions will strengthen gender-responsive labour policies, institutionalize gender mainstreaming, improve sex-disaggregated data, and promote equal pay and non-discrimination. Addressing structural barriers, including unequal care responsibilities, is essential to expanding women's access to decent work.
Advancing decent work in the care economy will generate employment while reducing gender inequality.
